title: Rapid Risk Reduction Pilot Kit: Economics, Positioning, and Security FAQ
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview:

This playbook is designed for Sales Engineers and Solutions teams running 30–90 day pilots with enterprise prospects where the primary buyer concern is risk reduction: latency predictability, data residency, and predictable unit economics. It bundles positioning, a concise competitive brief, three pricing scenarios for pilots, a one-page case study, pitch-deck talking points, and a targeted security FAQ to accelerate procurement and technical validation.

Goals and acceptance criteria (pilot):
1) Business success metrics (customer-defined):
   - P0: Integrated Redwood inference path in staging and processing representative workload.
   - P1: Measured 95th-percentile generation latency < 300ms for single-stream requests (model: rw-instruct-13b) under pilot traffic profile.
   - P2: Cost-per-1M-output-tokens estimate validated to +/- 15% after 2 weeks of representative traffic.
   - P3: Security checklist signed by customer security (encryption in transit/rest, KMS integration, logging).

2) Sales success metrics:
   - Pilot-to-paid conversion target: >= 60% within 90 days of pilot completion.
   - Decision maker consent: CTO, Head of Platform, and Security approver identified.

Value propositions / positioning (elevator and three-pronged brief):
- Elevator: "Redwood gives engineering teams production-grade LLM inference with predictable latency, clear unit economics, and enterprise-grade control. Run in our hosted cloud for fast time-to-value, or bring Redwood Dedicated/Private for regulated workloads."
- Three-pronged value for risk-focused buyers:
  1) Predictability: latency SLOs and deterministic autoscaling policies with canary fallback to smaller model variants.
  2) Cost transparency: token-level cost breakdowns in Redwood Console and pilot budgets that map to product metrics.
  3) Controls: VPC/private deployment, KMS/HSM key management, and per-route RBAC for auditability.

Competitive brief (one page):
- Primary competitors to frame vs: general cloud-managed endpoints (CLOUD-A endpoints), small LLM API vendors, and self-hosted inference stacks (OSS runtimes).
- Strengths to call out: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, intelligent batching and KV caching that empirically reduce per-token cost for conversational workloads, and integrated rollouts + tracing to avoid blind production regressions.
- Weaknesses to pre-empt: customers often ask about model choice/accuracy vs vendor X; position Redwood's model catalog and evaluation harness as the mitigation (we run benchmark sets and show quality/cost tradeoffs).

Quick competitive matrix (talking bullets):
- CLOUD-A managed endpoints: simple but limited fallback and higher tail latency under burst; fewer private deployment options.
- Vendor-B APIs: low entry cost but weaker observability and no reserved capacity SLA.
- OSS self-host: lower software license cost but large ops burden and slower time-to-value; limited unit economics analytics.

Pilot economics: three standard scenarios (examples, adjust to deal):
- Baseline PoC ("Developer Proof"): 30-day hosted pilot, up to 2M tokens total, free account credits cover first 200k tokens, additional tokens billed at pilot discounted rate. Estimated bill: $150–$450 (depending on model). Goal: validate integration and latency.
- Risk-Reduced Pilot ("Prod-lite"): 60-day pilot with reserved Dedicated pool (small allocation), peak throughput guarantee 50 rps, 20% reserved-capacity discount for pilot. Typical commit: $15,000 for 60 days (covers compute + support), reverts to consumption billing after pilot unless converted. Goal: validate SLOs and throughput for production.
- Strategic Private Proof ("Compliance-first"): 90-day Private deployment (VPC/on-prem), includes KMS integration, 1-day on-site install support, SOC2 report exchange, and custom legal addendum. Typical T&M: estimate $40k–$80k depending on packaging. Goal: complete security & procurement gate.

Pricing guidance and negotiation levers (for SEs):
- Use credits to remove friction for Developer Proof pilots.
- Offer time-limited reserved capacity at 15–25% discount to lock in predictable throughput.
- Include an "economics sandbox" session with customer engineers: run Redwood Console cost reports on representative traces to produce an accurate 12-month TCO comparison.
- Offer optional "Quality Safety Band" (QA-run prompts + regressions) as a billable add-on: $5k for a 2-week tailored eval and alert setup.

Pilot runbook (30–90 day):
1) Pre-kickoff (Sales + SE): identify success metrics, target models, and sample traffic. Obtain security questionnaire.
2) Kickoff week (days 0–7): grant pilot access, deploy example client SDK snippet, configure Redwood Console dashboards (latency, tokens, cost), and set up SLO alerts.
3) Validation phase (days 7–21): run smoke tests, transfer 10% realistic traffic or replay workloads, collect baseline cost and latency reports.
4) Stress and edge case (days 21–45): increased concurrency tests, failure injection (timeout/fallback), and canary rollout validation.
5) Close and convert (last 7–14 days): present final report (latency, cost, security signoffs), propose conversion path (Dedicated/Private contract or hosted consumption).

Pitch deck talking points (1-slide snippets):
- Slide: "Why Redwood for Production?" bullets: unified runtime, predictable latency, caching & batching economics, rollout controls.
- Slide: "Pilot Plan" bullets: duration, acceptance criteria (latency+cost+security), owner list, conversion options.
- Slide: "Cost Transparency" bullets: per-route token breakdowns, unit economics sandbox, expected pilot cost ranges.
- Slide: "Security & Compliance" bullets: SOC2, KMS/HSM, VPC & private control plane, audit logs export.

One-page case study (customer-friendly summary):
- Customer: FinLens (mid-market fintech) — use case: summarization and redaction for loan documents.
- Pilot scope: 60-day Risk-Reduced Pilot on Redwood Dedicated (rw-instruct-13b variant).
- Outcome: 95th PCT latency fell from 480ms (self-hosted baseline) to 220ms; estimated per-1M tokens cost reduced by 34% after enabling prefix caching and batching. Pilot converted to a paid Dedicated contract in 45 days.
- Testimonial quote (anonymized): "Redwood removed our ops uncertainty and delivered predictable latency under load — procurement cleared the private deployment in record time."

Security & compliance FAQ (targeted to pilots):
Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
A: Yes. Redwood supports KMS integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. For hosted pilots we provide envelope encryption and can enable KMIP/HSM on request.

Q: What evidence do you provide for security reviews?
A: We provide SOC2 Type II report excerpts, pen-test summaries, and a standard security questionnaire (SSQ) template. For Private deployments we produce architecture diagrams and runbook excerpts.

Q: How do you handle data residency and retention for pilot artifacts?
A: Pilot instances can be region-locked. Logs and telemetry retention can be limited to a pilot window (e.g., 30–90 days) and we provide exports for customer archival.

Q: How is PII handled in training/retention?
A: Redwood does not use customer data for model training unless explicitly contracted. For pilots, all inference request payloads are treated as transient and access-controlled.

Q: What controls exist for access and audit?
A: Per-route API keys, token-scoped roles, RBAC in Redwood Console, and audit logs with request/response metadata (excluding full raw content unless enabled). Logs can be streamed to customer SIEM via secure forwarding.

Q: What is the incident and escalation path during a pilot?
A: Assigned SE + customer success manager (CSM) are primary contacts. Critical incidents escalate to SRE oncall with a 1-hour response SLA for Dedicated pilots; hosted pilots use standard support channels with documented SLA tiers.

Operational checklist for security review (deliverable to customer security team):
- Architecture diagram (region, VPC peering, subnets)
- KMS integration plan and key rotation schedule
- Data flow and retention policy for pilot traces
- Logs export and SIEM integration plan
- Pen-test summary and SOC2 artifacts

Assets to attach to pilot packet (recommended):
- Short pitch deck (4 slides): Vision, Pilot Plan, Economics, Security & Next Steps
- One-page cost report template (CSV) and instructions
- Runbook snippet: how to reproduce latency benchmarks (curl examples and test harness instructions)
- Security questionnaire template and SOC2 excerpt
- Case study PDF of FinLens (anonymized)

Appendix: example commands and reporting snippets
- Example curl (hosted API):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-13b","input":"Summarize this loan document...","max_tokens":200}'

- Example Redwood Console report CSV columns:
  date,route,model,requests,total_input_tokens,total_output_tokens,cost_usd,median_latency_ms,p95_latency_ms

Notes and recommended next steps for field teams:
- When security concerns appear early, prioritize the Strategic Private Proof path and engage legal/security immediately.
- Use the economics sandbox before pricing concessions — real data reduces discount creep.
- Collect testimonialable metrics (latency reductions, cost delta, MTTI improvement) during pilot to accelerate procurement approval.
